summary:
In microgravity, a fire can appear completely extinguished while invisible "cool flames" keep burning silently, creating a critical hazard for spacecraft crews. Ghostfire is an interactive research tool built for NASA Space Apps’ Flame in Freefall challenge that lets users test spacecraft fire safety assumptions against real NASA experiments. 

Inside the Investigation Lab, users select a safety question, configure a mission environment, and explore evidence across eight NASA investigations. They can compare experimental conditions side by side, trace every finding directly to its primary NASA dataset or publication, and export a cited PDF evidence brief. Ghostfire highlights which findings support or challenge an assumption, flags where evidence is insufficient, and identifies which measurements could close the gap, helping engineers and crews see which fire detection signs they can actually trust.
details: Ghostfire is a web app we built for NASA Space Apps’ Flame in Freefall challenge. It helps users test spacecraft fire safety assumptions against real experiments. Our starting question was simple. If a flame disappears in microgravity, how can you tell whether combustion has stopped? In the Investigation Lab, users choose a question and a mission setting, such as the International Space Station or a lunar habitat. Ghostfire searches 10 evidence records from eight NASA investigations and ranks them by how directly they address the question, how closely the test conditions match, and how precisely the finding can be traced to its source. Users can see which findings support or challenge a preset assumption, compare two experiments side by side, and export a PDF brief with citations. For custom questions, Ghostfire retrieves relevant studies and leaves the conclusion to the reader. One of our favorite features is the three-frame sequence from the Cool Flames Investigation with Gases. Users can step through the hot flame, the dark interval, and the faint cool flame that appeared afterward. They can then open the finding, see how it was measured, and follow the citation to the original research. That connection between what users see and what the experiment actually measured is central to the project. We built Ghostfire with React, TypeScript, CSS, and Vite. The search and ranking run in the browser, and pdf-lib generates the evidence briefs. We used Playwright to test the investigation workflow on desktop and mobile and deployed the app to Cloudflare Pages. It runs in a standard web browser and requires no specialized hardware. Our team considered how gravity, fuel, oxygen, pressure, and airflow affect whether a finding applies to a different mission. We kept unknown conditions visible, separated observations from interpretations, and treated ranking scores as a guide to which studies to read first. Our goal is to help students, researchers, and engineers find relevant evidence faster and identify what they would still need to measure before making a spacecraft fire safety decision.
